text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: incoming error spike on /v1/generate with structured_output=true and function_call enabled. 5xx rate up 6x since 1802345400. Firing page to eng-oncall.

oncall-elena: on it. seeing increased p50 and p95 latency too? any specific model or region?

jay: logs show a surge of timeouts from 'function-invoke' stage; majority from hosted-api eu-west-1, ne 3rd-party model variants. Errors look like KV cache OOMs when structured output path and toolchains invoked.

anya: can we put a quick guard on structured output or function/tool calls? toggle feature flag to degrade to plain text for now.

sre-luca: +1. propose immediate emergency policy: for hosted tier free and trial accounts, block function_call and set structured_output_mode=plain for requests > 512 tokens. For others, soft-rate-limit function calls with 100rps global cap.

oncall-elena: I can apply hotpatch on the control plane. Two levers: 1) config service flag disable_function_calls=true 2) route-based token threshold. Which first?

backend-raj: do flag first, it's fastest. then apply rate-limiter rule to traffic-shaper if needed.

ops-platform: I'll open a short maintenance window in the console and annotate. tagging enterprise whitelist for later.

support-marc: if we disable function calls, some customers (payments-bot, doc-parser) will be impacted. Need rollout note to CSMs and broad customer message if it persists.

product-kim: we should whitelist enterprise Dedicated customers and key accounts. default degrade for anonymous and trials only.

oncall-elena: executing hotpatch now. patch command:
```
POST https://api.redwood-internal/configs/v1/hotpatch
Body: {"scope":"hosted","disable_function_calls":true,"structured_output_mode":"plain","token_threshold":512}
```

incident-bot: job 98321 started, config hotpatch in progress (ID 98321).

oncall-elena: applied. propagation reported to 95% by control-plane. Monitoring connectivity.

jay: traffic shaping metrics: function_call invocations dropped ~78% within 40s. overall 5xxs down 55% and p95 latency down 30% for affected cluster.

anya: good. any sign of cascading failures? background workers for tool execution had queued items — confirm backlog cleared?

sre-luca: backlog draining. we saw a spike in worker restarts earlier; restarted 3 pods with increased memory limits. Logged the restart reasons in the incident ticket.

support-marc: compiling list of customers with tool usage in last 24h. will send shortlist in 10m for comms.

product-kim: Decision: keep function_call disabled for trials/free and set structured_output to plain for all hosted until evening PDT. Whitelist enterprise dedicated and customers on SLA.

oncall-elena: putting an explicit rule in routing:
```
match: request.hosted AND account.tier in ["free","trial"]
actions: {
  disable_function_calls: true,
  structured_output_mode: "plain",
  rate_limit: 40rps
}
```

ops-platform: config committed and willary applied to 10% first then 100% after 2m; monitoring dashboard updated with annotation.

incident-bot: annotation added to incident #INC-2026-452.

jay: follow-up metric: token-cost per request dropped ~22% because of structured output fallback; good for unit economics but we still need to investigate root cause.

anya: root cause hypothesis: a regression in kernel memory accounting under certain kv-cache eviction patterns for structured-output codepath. creating repo issue and assigning to eng-runtime.

sre-luca: creating a mitigations playbook entry: if function_call errors > 4x baseline -> apply hosted-tier disable flag + structured_output plain fallback + 5m rate-limit.

support-marc: sending targeted email to affected customers now (drafted). noting that enterprise whitelists unaffected but some integrations may lose automation.

product-kim: we need post-incident follow-ups: rollback plan, ETA for proper fix, customer outreach. Also log any SLA impacts.

oncall-elena: I will keep the hotpatch for 4 hours and then do a controlled canary rollback after eng-runtime confirms fix or safe kernel bump. If errors remain low we can re-enable function calls for non-trials during the next business window.

backend-raj: starting deeper debug: capturing memory profiles and eviction traces with 30s sampling; will attach to ticket.

sre-luca: setting incident severity to Sev2 due to customer impact on automation for non-SLA customers. created pager rotation for escalation if it resurges.

incident-bot: Pager: oncall-elena acknowledged; escalation to oncall-jordan at 1802346900 if unresolved.

oncall-elena: handing off to jay for next 30m while I do customer comms with Marc. Jay, please watch for any new error clusters and be ready to tighten rate caps or apply additional routing to region eu-west-1.

jay: taking handoff. will watch dashboards and prepare rollback script to re-enable function_call if metrics look stable after runtime patch.

support-marc: confirm: message sent to 12 affected accounts + CSMs. included note about degraded automation and ETA for update.

product-kim: capture a postmortem template entry: "feature-guard used successfully to limit blast radius; tradeoff: degraded structured outputs for non-paid tiers; need longer-term fix in runtime and safer kernel accounting."

oncall-elena: closing slack thread for active mitigation; will update incident ticket with timeline and handoff notes.

jay: 10m check-in — no new spikes, errors holding at baseline. will remain watching.

sre-luca: adding retro action: add synthetic tests for structured_output + function_call under high-concurrency to catch regression earlier.

incident-bot: incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. next update in 1h or on change.

participants: incident-bot, oncall-elena, jay, anya, sre-luca, support-marc, backend-raj, product-kim, ops-platform
